# intRangeToCidr() function

Covers an integer address range with the fewest CIDR records that fit it exactly.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function intRangeToCidr(start: bigint, end: bigint, type: NetworkType, canonical?: boolean): string[];
```

**Returns:**

string\[\]

The records covering exactly `[start, end]` — no more and no less.

## Default Value

`canonical` defaults to `false`

## Remarks

The inverse of [cidrToRangeInt()](/api/net/latest/net.cidrtorangeint/)<!-- -->, and not a one-to-one one: an arbitrary range rarely aligns to a single prefix, so this splits it into the minimal set that does. A range already on a prefix boundary comes back as one record.

`type` is required here and cannot be inferred, for the same reason as in [intToIp()](/api/net/latest/net.inttoip/) — the integers alone do not say which family they are. The range is not validated, so an `end` below `start` yields an empty list rather than an error.
